page: Amazon Web Services c6in.16xlarge is a compute-optimized virtual instance built on the AWS Nitro hypervisor architecture. It features an Intel Xeon 8375C processor with 64 dedicated vCPUs (32 physical cores with 2 threads per core) running at a clock frequency of 3.5 GHz. The CPU package incorporates 54 MB of L3 cache alongside support for instruction sets including AVX-512 with VNNI, AES, VAES, and SHA-NI cryptography. Memory capacity is configured at 128.0 GB of DDR4 RAM running at 3 GHz, providing 2.0 GB per vCPU in alignment with standard compute-focused 1:2 allocations.

Network connectivity is a focal capability of this configuration, offering a baseline throughput of 100 Gbps without bundled local instance storage. It also lacks discrete hardware accelerators such as GPUs. All storage operations depend on network-attached EBS volumes, making optimal network utilization central to its input/output pipeline.

Benchmark results highlight strong parallel throughput across multiple disciplines. In multithreaded processing, the instance achieves top-quartile results in stress-ng multi-core testing, PassMark CPU score, Clang software compilation, ray tracing, and static web serving throughput reaching 45.26 GB/sec. Database operations in PassMark and medium-sized LLM inference generation also place in the upper tier. Conversely, single-threaded metrics, including Geekbench single-core, stress-ng single-core, and compression benchmarks, perform within the middle 50% baseline.

The 1:2 RAM-to-vCPU ratio and absence of bundled local storage represent key operational tradeoffs, demanding external volume management for persistent data. However, the pairing of 64 dedicated vCPUs with 100 Gbps network bandwidth yields high efficiency for distributed compute, high-traffic web serving layers, Clang-based CI/CD compilation, and network-heavy compute jobs.

It provides 128.0 GB of DDR4 memory, delivering a 2.0 GB per core ratio characteristic of compute-bound architectures. The instance includes a 100 Gbps baseline network interface, no local storage, and zero GPUs. Benchmark data demonstrates top-tier multi-core computing metrics, PassMark encryption and CPU extended instruction scores, alongside strong static web serving throughput and Clang software compilation. Given its combination of 64 dedicated threads and extensive 100 Gbps network bandwidth, c6in.16xlarge is structurally suited for scale-out distributed processing, continuous integration compilation pipelines, network-intensive workloads, and high-concurrency web tiers.
